title: British vs American English Words
summary: Discover everyday words that are different in British and American English. Learn how to use both correctly in conversation.

sections.p: When you talk about travel and cars, British and American English use very different words. For example, the area where you put your bags in a car is a boot in the UK, but it is called a trunk in the US. Knowing these differences helps you understand people from both countries easily.

ex.en: Put your heavy bags in the boot of the car.
ex.mean: Place your bags in the back storage area.

ex.en: I need to fill my car with gas before our long trip.
ex.mean: I need to put fuel in my vehicle.

sections.p: Inside and outside the home, people use different names for common items. If you want to go to the higher floor in a British building, you take the lift. In America, people call the exact same machine an elevator. The flat ground right outside your front door might be a garden in the UK, but Americans usually call it a yard.

ex.en: My apartment is on the fifth floor, so I always take the lift.
ex.mean: I use the moving room to go up to my home.

ex.en: We like to sit outside in the garden when the weather is warm.
ex.mean: We relax on the grass near our house.

sections.p: Buying clothes is another fun way to see how English changes across the ocean. When the weather gets cold, British people put on a jumper. Americans wear the same warm clothing item, but they call it a sweater. Also, the money you spend goes into your wallet or purse, which you might keep in your pocket.

ex.en: It is cold outside today, so wear your favourite jumper.
ex.mean: Put on your warm woolen top because of the cold.

ex.en: I love wearing comfortable sneakers when I walk to work.
ex.mean: I like wearing soft sports shoes for walking.

tip: Watch popular movies and TV shows from both the UK and the US. Notice the words the characters use for everyday objects to remember them better.

quiz.ask: Choose the correct British word for 'elevator'
quiz.en: My apartment is on the top floor, so I will take the ___.
It is cold outside, so please put on a warm ___.

quiz.ask: Choose the correct British word for 'apartment'
quiz.en: She lives in a small ___ near the city centre.
I need to buy a new pair of comfortable ___ for running.

quiz.ask: Choose the correct British word for 'car trunk'
quiz.en: Please put your suitcases in the ___ of the car.
We are planning a wonderful summer ___ to the beach.
